Right_EyeCenterX.blurb: Horizontal offset of the right eye (screen-right eye) in pixels from its nominal rest position. Positive moves it right on the LCD; negative left. Console range about −92…92 on Vector (half the 184 px face width).
Right_EyeCenterX.detail: Bound to s_faceDataOverride’s right-eye EyeCenterX via RegisterFaceWithConsoleVars (same loop that registers Left_*). Only changes what you see when ProcFace_Display is Override individually, and only if this value differs from the baseline captured when override mode / ResetFace last baselined. In Normal mode the animation keyframe wins. “Right” means the eye on the right side of the screen, not Vector’s anatomical right. Under Override together, left-eye params are copied onto the right eye every frame before draw — so editing Right_* alone has no visible effect in that mode; sculpt with Left_* (or switch to Override individually).
Right_EyeCenterX.howTo: 1) Set ProcFace_Display to Override individually (not Override together if you need independent right-eye control). 2) Optionally call ResetFace so the baseline matches the current animation face. 3) Nudge this value and watch the right eye slide horizontally.

Right_EyeCenterY.blurb: Vertical offset of the right eye in pixels from its nominal rest height. Positive moves it down on the LCD; negative up. Console range about −48…48 on Vector (half the 96 px face height).
Right_EyeCenterY.detail: Same override-only path as Right_EyeCenterX: registered on s_faceDataOverride right-eye EyeCenterY, applied in Display Override modes when different from baseline. Combined with EyeCenterX, EyeScale, and EyeAngle into the per-eye warp matrix before the eye polygon is drawn. Under Override together, left values overwrite this each frame.

Right_EyeScaleX.blurb: Horizontal scale of the right eye. 1.0 is nominal width (~43 px on Vector); larger makes that eye wider; 0 collapses it. Console range 0…10.
Right_EyeScaleX.detail: Override-face right EyeScaleX. Applied only under ProcFace_Display Override modes when changed from baseline — and under Override together the left-eye scale is forced onto the right eye, so use Override individually for independent width. Independent of whole-face ProcFace_ScaleX. Multiplies NominalEyeWidth when building the eye polygon and transform.

Right_EyeScaleY.blurb: Vertical scale of the right eye. 1.0 is nominal height (~57 px on Vector); larger makes that eye taller; 0 flattens it. Console range 0…10.
Right_EyeScaleY.detail: Same override path as Right_EyeScaleX. LookAt and blink code also touch EyeScaleY on the live face; under override you freeze/sculpt via console instead of those systems for any param that differs from baseline. Override together copies Left_EyeScaleY onto the right eye.

Right_EyeAngle.blurb: Rotation of the right eye alone, in degrees, around that eye’s center. Positive and negative tilt the eye shape (and its lids/hotspot) like a cocked eyebrow. Console range −360…360.
Right_EyeAngle.detail: Maps to right-eye EyeAngle on the override ProceduralFace. Only visible under ProcFace_Display Override modes when different from baseline. Fed into GetTransformationMatrix with scale and center; does not rotate the whole face (use ProcFace_Angle_deg for that). Under Override together, Left_EyeAngle is copied to the right eye before draw.

Right_LowerInnerRadiusX.blurb: How rounded the lower-inner corner of the right eye is, as a fraction of half-eye width (0 = sharp corner, 1 = fully rounded to the eye midline). Console range 0…1.
Right_LowerInnerRadiusX.detail: “Inner” means toward the nose / face center — for the screen-right eye that is the lower-left corner of that eye’s polygon (geometry is authored in left-eye coords then mirrored: x is negated for WhichEye::Right). Multiplied by halfEyeWidth for ellipse2Poly. Override-only (with ProcFace_Display Override modes) when changed from baseline. Pair with Right_LowerInnerRadiusY for the vertical radius of the same corner. Under Override together, left-eye radii overwrite these.

Right_LowerInnerRadiusY.blurb: Vertical radius of the lower-inner (toward-nose) corner of the right eye, as a fraction of half-eye height. 0 = sharp; 1 = very round. Console range 0…1.
Right_LowerInnerRadiusY.detail: Paired with Right_LowerInnerRadiusX. Both must be > 0 for a curved corner; if either is 0 the drawer places a hard corner vertex instead of an ellipse arc.

Right_UpperInnerRadiusX.blurb: Horizontal rounding of the upper-inner (toward-nose) corner of the right eye, as a fraction of half-eye width. 0 = sharp; 1 = fully rounded. Console range 0…1.
Right_UpperInnerRadiusX.detail: For the screen-right eye this is the upper-left corner of that eye after the left-authored poly is mirrored. Same override path as other radius params. Drawn with cv::ellipse2Poly using ProcFace_EllipseDelta as angular step.

Right_UpperInnerRadiusY.blurb: Vertical rounding of the upper-inner corner of the right eye, as a fraction of half-eye height. Console range 0…1.
Right_UpperInnerRadiusY.detail: Paired with Right_UpperInnerRadiusX. Both > 0 required for a curved arc; otherwise a hard corner.

Right_UpperOuterRadiusX.blurb: Horizontal rounding of the upper-outer corner of the right eye (away from the nose — right side of the right eye on screen), as a fraction of half-eye width. Console range 0…1.
Right_UpperOuterRadiusX.detail: “Outer” = toward the edge of the face. Same override + ellipse2Poly path as other corner radii. Useful for soft vs squared upper lids on the outer edge. Override together still replaces right with left before draw.

Right_UpperOuterRadiusY.blurb: Vertical rounding of the upper-outer corner of the right eye, as a fraction of half-eye height. Console range 0…1.
Right_UpperOuterRadiusY.detail: Paired with Right_UpperOuterRadiusX for the upper-right corner of the screen-right eye polygon (after mirror).

Right_LowerOuterRadiusX.blurb: Horizontal rounding of the lower-outer corner of the right eye (outer/lower-right of that eye on screen), as a fraction of half-eye width. Console range 0…1.
Right_LowerOuterRadiusX.detail: Same override path as other radii. Outer = away from nose. Zero either X or Y radius of this corner → sharp vertex instead of arc.

Right_LowerOuterRadiusY.blurb: Vertical rounding of the lower-outer corner of the right eye, as a fraction of half-eye height. Console range 0…1.
Right_LowerOuterRadiusY.detail: Paired with Right_LowerOuterRadiusX for the lower-right corner of the screen-right eye.

Right_UpperLidY.blurb: How far the upper eyelid of the right eye closes. 0 = fully open (lid at top of eye); 1 = fully closed (lid reaches the bottom). Console range 0…1.
Right_UpperLidY.detail: Builds an upper-lid polygon that is filled black over the eye shape (negative space). Multiplied by NominalEyeHeight for pixel drop. Override-only under ProcFace_Display Override modes when changed from baseline. Combine with UpperLidAngle / UpperLidBend for squint, wink, or arched lids on the right eye only (use Override individually for a one-eye wink; Override together copies left lids onto right).

Right_UpperLidAngle.blurb: Tilts the right eye’s upper lid line in degrees. Positive/negative angles make one side of the lid drop more than the other (asymmetric squint). Console range −45…45.
Right_UpperLidAngle.detail: Used as tan(angle) to raise/lower the lid corners relative to each other, and as the rotation for the optional lid-bend ellipse. Lid polygons are warped with the same left-authored then mirrored path as the eye outline. Override-only path with other Right_* sculpt params; ineffective under Override together when left overwrites right.

Right_UpperLidBend.blurb: Curves the right upper lid. 0 = straight lid edge; positive bends the lid down into the eye (soft droop); negative bends up away from the eye (arched). Console range −1…1.
Right_UpperLidBend.detail: Non-zero values add an ellipse2Poly arc to the upper-lid polygon. Negative bend uses fillPoly (concave) instead of fillConvexPoly. Scale is fraction of NominalEyeHeight. Override-only under ProcFace_Display Override modes.

Right_LowerLidY.blurb: How far the lower eyelid of the right eye closes. 0 = fully open (lid at bottom of eye); 1 = fully closed (lid reaches the top). Console range 0…1.
Right_LowerLidY.detail: Mirror of UpperLidY for the bottom lid: polygon filled black over the eye. Useful for tired looks, blinks, or lower squint on the right eye alone. Override-only when ProcFace_Display is in an Override mode and the value differs from baseline; Override together still forces left→right.

Right_LowerLidAngle.blurb: Tilts the right eye’s lower lid line in degrees. Console range −45…45.
Right_LowerLidAngle.detail: Same geometry role as UpperLidAngle but for the lower-lid polygon and its bend arc. Override-only path.

Right_LowerLidBend.blurb: Curves the right lower lid. 0 = straight; positive bends up into the eye; negative bends down away from the eye. Console range −1…1.
Right_LowerLidBend.detail: Non-zero adds an ellipse arc to the lower-lid poly; negative bend uses non-convex fillPoly. Fraction of NominalEyeHeight. Override-only under ProcFace_Display Override modes.

Right_Lightness.blurb: Brightness multiplier for the filled right-eye pixels only. 1 = full strength; 0 blacks out that eye; values between dim it. Console range −1…1 (product faces use about 0…1; −1 is an animation “unset” sentinel).
Right_Lightness.detail: Applied in DrawEye after the global ProcFace_EyeLightnessMultiplier: each lit eye pixel is multiplied by this value. Only affects the display when ProcFace_Display is Override individually/together and this differs from the override baseline — but under Override together left Lightness is copied onto the right, so dimming only the right eye requires Override individually. Does not change hue (use ProcFace_Hue) or the CRT scanline path. Extreme negatives clamp toward black after cast.

Right_HotSpotCenterX.blurb: Horizontal position of the soft bright “hotspot” (pupil-like glow) inside the right eye, as a fraction of eye width. 0 = eye center; −1 = left edge; +1 = right edge. Console range −1…1.
Right_HotSpotCenterX.detail: Only visible when ProcFace_HotspotRender is on (otherwise eyes are flat fill). The hotspot center is warped with the same eye transform as the polygon, so it moves/rotates with Right_EyeAngle and scale. Override-only for the sculpt value itself under ProcFace_Display Override modes. Falloff width is global ProcFace_HotspotFalloff. Under Override together, Left_HotSpotCenterX is forced onto the right eye.
Right_HotSpotCenterX.howTo: 1) Enable ProcFace_HotspotRender. 2) Set ProcFace_Display to Override individually (or together if you want left hotspot mirrored to both). 3) Move this X (and Right_HotSpotCenterY) to place the bright core in the right eye only when using Override individually.

Right_HotSpotCenterY.blurb: Vertical position of the right eye’s soft hotspot, as a fraction of eye height. 0 = center; −1 = top edge; +1 = bottom edge. Console range −1…1.
Right_HotSpotCenterY.detail: Paired with Right_HotSpotCenterX. Same requires: ProcFace_HotspotRender for the glow to paint, and ProcFace_Display Override modes for this console value to replace the animation’s hotspot when it differs from baseline. Override together copies left hotspot onto right.
